capabilities.name: Wall / Door / Window / Column / Slab instance recovery from Revit 2024 partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records + partition_schema_mvp::instances_from_partition_category_records / slabs_from_partition_category_records + partition_ifc_export_overrides; tests/project_count_fixtures.rs (IFCWALL 360/360, IFCDOOR 132/132, IFCWINDOW 6/6, IFCCOLUMN 256/256, IFCSLAB 80/80, IFCSHADINGDEVICE 20/20, tolerance 0) and the magnetar-2024-core-interior-slim OctetProof verdict, where entity_counts.IFCWALL / IFCDOOR / IFCWINDOW / IFCCOLUMN / IFCSLAB / IFCSHADINGDEVICE are all inside the claimed surface and rvt-rs, IfcOpenShell and IFClite agree exactly
capabilities.notes: Scope is six BuiltInCategories (OST_Walls, OST_Doors, OST_Windows, OST_Columns, OST_Floors, OST_BuildingPad), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. Selection is a direct byte test, not a heuristic: the record must carry no container reference at +0x32 and placement kind 0xffffef7f at +0x42 (RE-21). It supersedes the #204 column rule, whose family-local bbox proxy and highest-ElementId-per-footprint collapse are removed. RE-22 (#212) extended the same rule to slabs and found it already exact there: its 99 OST_Floors selections are all exported (79 IfcSlab + 20 IfcShadingDevice), and the 80th exported slab is an OST_BuildingPad (Pad:Site Pad, ElementId 21975). The IfcSlab / IfcShadingDevice split is a per-instance Revit 'IFC Export As' override read out of the partition parameter block: the UTF-16LE value string with the owning ElementId as a u64 at -0x0dc and again at -0x11e, both required to agree and to be declared in Global/ElemTable. Thirty-one entries pass on this file, naming 21 ids; the 20 that are also placed instances are exactly the export's IFCSHADINGDEVICE Tag set. Only IfcShadingDevice is honoured as an override target — an unrecognised value leaves the element on its class mapping. Where one ElementId is framed more than once, the record with the greatest bounding-box z extent is kept; that agrees with the export's IfcExtrudedAreaSolid.Depth on 79 of 80 slabs (the 80th is exported as two stacked solids summing to it). Ties go to the newest frame - the greatest (stream, offset) - because Revit rewrites an edited element into a higher-numbered Partitions stream and leaves the earlier copy in place (RE-26): 171 of 360 walls and 96 of 132 doors carry two frames that disagree about the plan box, and on the newest one the wall's thin plan extent equals the nominal thickness of the IfcWallType Revit's export assigns on 360 of 360 (201 of 360 on the oldest) and its type slot equals that IfcWallType.Tag on 356 of 360 (183 of 360 on the oldest; the positional read is superseded by RE-28's set test, which is 360 of 360 - see element-record-wall-type-join). Global/ElemTable's u32 at +0x1c is a monotone version counter that ranks the same way across all 976 exported instances. No frame of any instance on this file disagrees about the box's z, so the tie-break cannot move an element between storeys - storey_bound_elements was 801 either way when this was measured, and is 853 since #219 / RE-27. Column, window, slab and building-pad boxes are unchanged; door boxes move without a measurement that adjudicates them, since a door's record box is not the panel Revit exports and 0 of 132 are world-exact either way. Bodies are the record's own bounding box, not a recovered family profile or wall location curve; for plates the z extent is the real thickness, and since RE-25 (#31) the plan profile of a slab whose sketch closes is the recovered sketch boundary rather than the box rectangle - see element-record-slab-plan-profile. Base/top Level ElementIds stay unbound (#86); doors and windows are attached to their host wall as of RE-23/#222 (see element-record-door-window-host-binding). Storey containment came from the #213 column-derived elevation set when this row landed: walls, doors and columns bound by their record base, plates by their record top face (Revit hangs a floor below its level) — 51 of 100 plates bound and all 51 agreed with the export, none wrongly, while windows never bound because their record base is a sill height, measured 0 of 6. Since #219 / RE-27 the first join tried is the Level ElementId the record itself names, which reaches all 100 plates and all 6 windows; that elevation path survives as the fallback - see record-level-reference-storey-bind. This is not evidence for any other category or release.
capabilities.user_impact: On the recorded Revit 2024 project, walls, doors, windows, architectural columns, floor slabs and building pads come out as placed IFC entities with position, a solid body and (for slabs) a measured thickness and plan profile, matching Revit's own export element for element. On Autodesk's Snowdon Towers 2024 samples most element frames use a second prologue; their ElementIds come from the enclosing partition record (RE-35), and walls, doors, windows, columns and floors export under Revit's own ids (see element-records-second-prologue-ids). Structural framing, structural columns, foundations and generic models export from the same records (see element-records-structural-categories).

capabilities.name: Furniture, casework, fixtures, equipment, ceilings, curtain-wall parts, railings, wall sweeps, ducts and pipes from partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::PRODUCT_RECORD_CATEGORIES; tests/element_records_2025.rs against Drshelden/IFC-ECS RE1 Architecture, Mechanical and Plumbing (MIT, fetched by CI tier 2); examples/probe_re33_category_census.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-33-product-categories.md
capabilities.notes: Thirteen more BuiltInCategory values decode under the unchanged RE-21 instance rule, and every ElementId they select from a record carrying it at +0x00 is a Tag in Revit's own export of the same file: zero false positives on RE1 Architecture, Mechanical and Plumbing (Revit 2025) and on Snowdon Towers (Revit 2024, measured locally). With RE-35's second-prologue ids, RE1 Architecture exports all 58 elements of these categories, RE1 Mechanical all 66 ducts, pipes and fittings and RE1 Plumbing all 117 pipes and fittings and all 6 fixtures, plus one fixture Revit's export leaves out; on Snowdon, curtain panels, railings, ceilings, furniture and fixtures are complete, and 47 curtain panels are elements Revit's export omits (#309). The 60 placed instances with no 3D volume are left out as Revit leaves them out. Second-prologue frames keep the container and placement fields, so the unattributed count covers placed instances only and matches the missing elements exactly for pipes, fittings, mullions, columns, railings, ceilings and furniture. Bodies are the record bounding box; entities are the IFC4 types (IfcFurniture, IfcSanitaryTerminal, IfcCovering, IfcMember, IfcPlate, IfcRailing, IfcBuildingElementProxy, IfcDuctSegment, IfcDuctFitting, IfcPipeSegment, IfcPipeFitting). Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Revit 2024 and 2025 projects export furniture, casework, plumbing fixtures, specialty equipment, ceilings, curtain-wall mullions and panels, railings, wall sweeps, ducts and pipes whose records carry their ElementId, each one an element Revit's own export also holds; the diagnostics count the rest.

capabilities.name: ElementIds for second-prologue partition element records, read from the enclosing partition record
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::partition_record_chain / assign_second_prologue_ids / RevitFile::second_prologue_ids; tests/partition_record_chain.rs (every first-prologue frame starts a record of its own id on Core Interior and the RE1 models); tests/element_records_2025.rs; examples/probe_re35_record_wrapper.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-35-partition-record-wrapper.md; reports/element-framing/RE-43-invalid-element-id.md
capabilities.notes: Every Partitions/* stream opens with a chain of records, one per element: u64 ElementId, u32 size, u16 prologue constant (release constant + 28), u16 count, the body, and a 16-byte trailer that repeats the size (RE-35). A first-prologue frame starts its record; a second-prologue frame (RE-30) sits inside its element's record, so its ElementId is the record's, read rather than inferred. All 30,432 first-prologue frames across nine 2024 and 2025 files start a record of their own id, and the chains hold every declared id on Core Interior and the RE1 models. Records after the chain belong to loaded families' own documents and never export. Against Revit's own exports: RE1 Architecture, Mechanical and Plumbing reach 100% of every recovered entity; Snowdon Towers Architectural exports 6,045 elements, 5,945 in Revit's export (a frame holding u32::MAX, the invalid ElementId, also takes its record's id, RE-43), with every wall, column, door, window, curtain wall and panel, railing, ceiling, furniture item, fixture and generic model of Revit's export attributed once RE-41 declares the ElemTable's second id. The rest are real elements Revit's export leaves out (#309); the 18 in non-primary design options are left out as Revit leaves them out (RE-40). Floors, building pads and ceilings get their ids too. It replaces RE-34's reference-order inference, which gave a door its type's id on a Revit 2025 file outside its hold-outs. Placed instances with no 3D volume are left out, as Revit leaves them out. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Files whose element records mostly lack an ElementId at their start (Autodesk's Snowdon Towers samples, the RE1 models, projects saved incrementally) export their walls, doors, windows, floors, ceilings, columns, curtain-wall parts, railings, furniture, fixtures, ducts and pipes under the ElementIds Revit itself uses; the diagnostics count what is still left out.

capabilities.name: ElemTable records whose two ids differ declare the second
capabilities.evidence: elem_table::declared_ids; examples/probe_re41_elem_table_secondary_ids.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-41-elem-table-secondary-ids.md
capabilities.notes: A 40-byte Global/ElemTable record carries two u32 ids, at +16 and +36. They agree on every record of Core Interior, the RE1 models, teste_export_2025, Projeto1 and the 2016-2023 projects measured. On Autodesk's Snowdon Towers samples (local only) they differ on 84 records (Architectural) and 27 (Structural); there the second is the id of the element's partition record (RE-35) and the Tag Revit's own IFC export writes, and the first is neither. The declared id set now holds both (a 0 in the second is not added), which attributes all 37 element records Snowdon Architectural left unattributed (16 walls, 4 columns, 17 generic models, all in Revit's export) and one floor on Snowdon Structural (in the VIM export). Licensed files export byte-identically. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Elements whose ElemTable record carries a second id, such as those in a primary design option on Autodesk's sample, export under the ElementId Revit itself uses instead of being counted as unattributed.

capabilities.name: Structural framing, structural columns, structural foundations and generic models from partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::PRODUCT_RECORD_CATEGORIES (OST_StructuralFraming, OST_StructuralColumns, OST_StructuralFoundation, OST_GenericModel); examples/probe_re36_vim_oracle.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-36-structural-categories.md
capabilities.notes: Four more BuiltInCategory values decode under the RE-21 instance rule with RE-35's enclosing-record ElementIds and export as IfcBeam (.BEAM.), IfcColumn (.COLUMN.), IfcFooting and IfcBuildingElementProxy. Measured locally on Autodesk's Snowdon Towers 2024 samples, which have no licence and are not in CI. Against the VIM export of the Structural sample (a later edition), every exported id the VIM carries has the record's category there: 914 framing members, 74 columns, 90 foundations and 91 generic models, none under another category. The 28 framing ids it lacks are beam-system members the later edition regenerated. On the architectural sample 260 of 261 generic models are in Revit's own IFC4 export; the other is in a non-primary design option. Framing on that file has no braces (Structural Usage: joists, girders, purlins), so IfcBeam is the entity; a brace would also export as IfcBeam, since the record's structural type is not decoded, and Revit's own PredefinedType is not measured. Rebar, structural connections and beam systems have correct ids but are not exported. Bodies are the record bounding box. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Revit 2024 and 2025 structural models export their beams, joists, girders, columns, footings and generic models as IFC elements under Revit's own ElementIds, with bounding-box bodies; rebar and connections are not exported.

capabilities.name: Lighting fixtures, air terminals, food-service equipment, site elements, elevators and ramps from partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::PRODUCT_RECORD_CATEGORIES; tests/element_records_2025.rs against Drshelden/IFC-ECS RE1 Mechanical and Electrical (MIT, fetched by CI tier 2); reports/element-framing/RE-37-fixture-site-circulation-categories.md
capabilities.notes: Nine more BuiltInCategory values (OST_LightingFixtures, OST_DuctTerminal, OST_FoodServiceEquipment, OST_Planting, OST_Parking, OST_Entourage, OST_Hardscape, OST_VerticalCirculation, OST_Ramps) decode under the RE-21 instance rule with RE-35's enclosing-record ElementIds. Every exported element is a Tag of Revit's own export with none outside it, and each entity is complete: 447 lighting fixtures, 26 food-service items, 157 planting, parking, entourage and hardscape proxies, 2 ramps and 2 elevators on Snowdon Towers (local only); 7 air terminals on RE1 Mechanical; 12 lighting fixtures on RE1 Electrical. Entities follow Revit's IFC4 export on Snowdon (IfcLightFixture, IfcElectricAppliance, IfcBuildingElementProxy, IfcTransportElement, IfcRamp); air terminals use IfcAirTerminal, the IFC4 subtype of the IfcFlowTerminal Revit writes in IFC2x3. Electrical fixtures and lighting devices are measured but not added because Revit's export omits some of them; slab edges are added by RE-40 once non-primary design options are left out; fire alarm and data devices and electrical and mechanical equipment wait for an IFC4 reference; stairs and roofs are RE-39. Bodies are the record bounding box. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Revit 2024 and 2025 projects export their lighting fixtures, air terminals, kitchen equipment, planting, parking, entourage, hardscape, elevators and ramps as the IFC entities Revit itself uses, each one an element Revit's own export also holds.

capabilities.name: Stairs as IFC aggregates of their runs, landings and stringers, and roofs
capabilities.evidence: partition_schema_mvp::attach_aggregate_wholes; IfcEntity::Aggregate and the STEP writer's IfcRelAggregates; examples/probe_re39_stair_parts.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-39-stair-aggregates.md
capabilities.notes: A stair's runs, landings and stringers name the stair's ElementId in their reference lists. Each stair exports as a bodiless IfcStair and its parts (IfcStairFlight, IfcSlab .LANDING., IfcMember .STRINGER.) are related to it by IfcRelAggregates, not contained in a storey. Measured locally on Snowdon Towers Architectural, which has no licence and is not in CI: the same 26 stairs aggregate as in Revit's IFC4 export, and every one of the 228 parts rvt-rs attaches is in the matching Revit aggregate; all 256 new elements (27 stairs, 42 flights, 17 landings, 170 stringers) are in Revit's export. Railings stay standalone: Revit aggregates 65 of the 70 that name a stair, and nothing read tells the other five apart. PredefinedTypes are left unset. Roofs (OST_Roofs) export as one IfcRoof each with the record box: all 20 Snowdon roofs are IfcRoof Tags in Revit's export, which decomposes 7 of them into a same-Tag IfcSlab .ROOF. part that rvt-rs does not reproduce. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Stairs come out as Revit exports them: one IfcStair per stair holding its flights, landings and stringers, so IFC viewers show and select a stair as one assembly.

capabilities.name: Design options: leave out non-primary options, and slab edges
capabilities.evidence: partition_design_options::compute_design_options; PartitionElementRecord::design_option; examples/probe_re40_design_options.rs; tests/design_options.rs (the licensed files read no design option); reports/element-framing/RE-40-design-option-primary.md
capabilities.notes: An element record holds its design option's ElementId at +0x2a. A design option set's partition record lists its options at +0x56, and the set's name entry repeats that list and closes with the primary option's ElementId. The exporter drops records in a set's other options, as Revit's IFC export does by default, and reports them as the skipped item element_record_in_non_primary_design_option. A set whose name entry is missing or ambiguous stays unresolved and its options are kept. Measured locally on Snowdon Towers Architectural, which has no licence and is not in CI: of the placed instances of recovered categories, the 29 in the primary option 2059970 are all in Revit's IFC4 export and the 27 in non-primary options are all missing from it; removing them takes the elements outside Revit's export from 118 to 100 and removes none it holds. Slab edges (OST_EdgeSlab) are added as IfcBuildingElementProxy: all 59 exported are in Revit's export. No licensed file has a design option. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Projects with design options export the model Revit itself exports, the main model with each option set's primary option, instead of every option stacked on top of each other.

capabilities.name: Family and type names of element-record elements, from partition name entries
capabilities.evidence: partition_names::find_name_entries / resolve_type / resolve_family; RevitFile::element_names; tests/element_names.rs against 2024_Core_Interior_slim.ifc and the RE1 exports (CI tier 2); examples/probe_re38_names.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-38-family-and-type-names.md; examples/probe_re42_nested_families.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-42-nested-families.md
capabilities.notes: Revit 2024 and 2025 partitions carry a name entry for every loaded family and family type: u64 ElementId, u32 length, UTF-16 name, i64 BuiltInCategory. An element's type is the one reference-list id of its own category with an entry, and its family is the one such id in the type's partition record (RE-35); where that record also names families nested in the type's family, the family is the one candidate whose own record names all the others (RE-42). The IFC Name becomes Family:Type:ElementId and the ObjectType Family:Type, as in Revit's export, and the property set gains FamilyName and TypeName. Every name written equals Revit's for the same Tag: 394 on Core Interior, 3,831 on Snowdon Towers (plus 71 elements Revit's export omits), 56, 42, 60 and 12 on RE1 Architecture, Mechanical, Plumbing and Electrical (plus one each omitted on Architecture and Plumbing), 1 on teste_export_2025. On the Snowdon structural sample 1,132 of the 1,156 named elements in the VIM export equal its family and type; the other 24 are a type the VIM's later edition renamed. On Snowdon the name table agrees with the VIM export on all 348 shared ids, name and category. System families (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, stairs, railings, curtain walls) have no name entry and keep Class-ElementId names and no ObjectType; their type names come from the type's own element data (RE-44, element-record-system-type-names). Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Doors, windows, columns, furniture, fixtures, mullions, panels and other family instances show the same Family:Type names in the IFC and the viewer that Revit gives them.

capabilities.name: Type names of system-family elements (walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, railings), from the type's element data
capabilities.evidence: partition_names::element_data_header / find_element_data_names; partition_type_records::scan_type_records (2024 and 2025, second-prologue records); partition_schema_mvp::recover_partition_schema_mvp; tests/element_names.rs core_interior_system_type_names_are_revits and re1_system_type_names_are_revits (CI tier 2); examples/probe_re44_system_type_names.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-44-system-type-names.md
capabilities.notes: A system-family type has no RE-38 name entry. Its serialised element data opens with ff ff ff ff, a u16 header word (0x02d3 on Revit 2024, 0x02ef on Revit 2025), 01 00 00 00 and the type's u64 ElementId, and its name is the first framed string after that (ff ff ff ff, a u16 tag other than 0xffff, a u32 length, UTF-16). An element's type is the one type-definition record of its own category its reference list names (RE-28); on Snowdon and RE1 most such records are second-prologue frames that take their partition record's id (RE-35), and on 2025 they carry the 2025 marker and prologue constant. The element's property set gains TypeName. Every name written equals the type half of Revit's ObjectType for the same Tag: 460 on Core Interior (360 walls, 99 floors, the pad), 1,545 on Snowdon Towers Architectural, 16 on RE1 Architecture, 1 on Projeto1, and 6 of 7 on teste_export_2025, where the seventh wall's frame, data and bounding box all describe the other type, so that export was made from a later state of the model. The system family's own name (Basic Wall, Floor) is not stored in the file - the Portuguese export writes Parede basica for the same family - so no FamilyName is written, the IFC Name stays Class-ElementId and ObjectType stays unset. Types with no element-data block stay unnamed: RE1's one railing type and 7 of 22 Snowdon railing types. No IfcWallType or IfcSlabType entity and no IfcRelDefinesByType is written, and no other field of the type's data is read. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Walls, floors, ceilings, roofs and railings show the type name Revit gives them (for example 8" Interior Partition 3 Hour or Basement Slab) in the IFC property set and the viewer.

capabilities.name: Revit's IFC export overrides (Export to IFC As, IFC Predefined Type, and their type-level twins), from element data
capabilities.evidence: partition_ifc_export_overrides::find_export_parameters / scan_export_parameters / ExportParameters; ifc::category_map::lookup_export_override / predefined_type_for; tests/ifc_export_overrides.rs (CI tier 2); examples/probe_re45_ifc_export_parameters.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-45-ifc-export-parameters.md
capabilities.notes: Revit's four IFC export parameters are entries i64 BuiltInParameter, u32 n, UTF-16 value in an element's serialised data: IFC_EXPORT_ELEMENT_AS (-1019014), IFC_EXPORT_ELEMENT_TYPE_AS (-1019015), IFC_EXPORT_PREDEFINEDTYPE (-1019016) and IFC_EXPORT_PREDEFINEDTYPE_TYPE (-1019017), public BuiltInParameter values. An entry belongs to the declared element whose element-data header (RE-44) is the last one before it, at most 0x800 bytes back (0x1ac measured); a value must have the shape of an IFC entity name or an enumerator. An element exports as its own override, else its type's (IfcCoveringType naming IfcCovering), with its own predefined type, else its type's, written only when it is an IFC4 enumerator of that entity. Honoured entities are the ones a reference export demonstrates: IfcShadingDevice (RE-22), IfcSlab and IfcCovering. Measured: on Core Interior every element rvt-rs writes has Revit's entity, and floors 20912 and 70325, which carry ifcSlab with ROOF, are IFCSLAB .ROOF. as in Revit's export (previously .FLOOR.); on teste_export_2025 (local only) the three walls of type 402, which carries IfcCoveringType with CLADDING, are IFCCOVERING .CLADDING. as in Revit's (previously IFCWALL). RE1, Snowdon Towers, Einhoven and Projeto1 carry no export parameter. The owners of IfcShadingDevice equal RE-22's owner-offset read, which no longer feeds the export. IfcSpace and IfcFooting overrides exist on Core only on elements Revit does not export and stay unhonoured. Revit's own category-to-entity mapping table is not read, and no IfcSlabType or IfcCoveringType is written. Revit 2024 and 2025.
capabilities.user_impact: Elements a modeller set to export as another IFC entity or predefined type - a roof-like floor, a wall used as cladding - come out of rvt-rs as they do out of Revit.

capabilities.name: Curtain walls from Revit 2024 and 2025 element records: the walls their mullions name, aggregating their panels and mullions
capabilities.evidence: partition_schema_mvp::attach_curtain_walls / CURTAIN_WALL_CLASS / CURTAIN_WALL_PART_CLASSES; ifc::category_map (CurtainWall -> IFCCURTAINWALL .NOTDEFINED.); tests/curtain_walls.rs against RE1 Architecture (CI tier 2); examples/probe_re46_curtain_walls.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-46-curtain-walls.md

capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_SketchLines, -2000045), one release band (Revit 2024), one recorded edge, and only the plates the RE-22 instance rule already recovers. The join is exact and byte-anchored: the last slot of the second counted reference list at +0x88 names the sketched element, and the 3688 sketch-line records on 2024_Core_Interior.rvt name 126 owners including all 80 exported IFCSLAB and all 20 exported IFCSHADINGDEVICE ids.
